question: Aman and Pawan together invested ₹62,800 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹11,600, Pawan's share was ₹2,900. What was the difference between their investments?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the time of investment is the same, Investment Ratio = Profit Ratio.

Pawan's profit ratio = 2900 ÷ 11600 = 1/4 of total profit.

Aman's profit ratio = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4 of total profit.

Difference in ratio = 3/4 − 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2 of total.

Difference in investment = 1/2 × 62800 = ₹31,400.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹31,400.**
